recent: the operating booth of a small vintage planetarium before a community costume evening, a compact hand-cranked pinhole star projector and curved dark ceiling dotted with a few unlabelled projected stars; warm practical lamps, no science laboratory or live-music stage — she patiently aligns a tiny star projector, an everyday echo of the dying stars from which her element came. Reaching upward to turn two small shutter knobs makes the short hem of her fitted costume bolero rise, exposing an unplanned band of midriff above the high-waisted playsuit bottom; the neckline and shoulder bands stay secure. The story is her precise, absorbed adjustment of a tiny device, not ornamental regalia

an empty nostalgic bowling alley just before opening, polished wooden lanes in soft morning light and a low mechanical ball-return rail with one dense charcoal-black ball; no readable scores, signs or numerals — at an adult retro costume club event she tries to coax an unexpectedly heavy bowling ball out of the return cradle, amused that an ordinary pastime has become a small exercise in managing dense weight. As she lowers into a stable squat, the concertina pleats of her short outer apron fan apart over the fully opaque fitted shorts, showing more upper leg through movement, with no wind, wet fabric, undone fasteners or slipped shoulder strap

a quiet apartment's luggage-packing nook at early morning, an open hard-sided suitcase lined with thick folded towels on a low bench, plain shelves and soft window light; no laboratory, garden, palace or waterfront — she carefully settles a surprisingly heavy antique green-glass serving bowl into the padded suitcase, taking the same care with a household heirloom that she would with immense contained power. A loose asymmetric hip drape has caught on the suitcase handle as she crouches, lifting the outer drape at one side and revealing the fully opaque gathered shorts beneath; she pauses with a small amused look at this mundane snag

Her sunny apartment breakfast nook with an old wooden roller blind, a low broad step stool and a teacup cooling on the windowsill; the city rooftops lie outside, with a small box of spare rubber bands on the table — She repairs a roller blind whose return mechanism has lost its rubber tension band. One hand holds the wooden bottom rail while the other stretches a replacement rubber band onto a small hook. Reaching upward draws the loose short camisole hem above her waist for a moment, exposing her midriff while the opaque lingerie-inspired shorts and bodice remain securely in place; her expression is amused concentration

A bright community pool rooftop greenhouse after swim practice, with a potting tray, small herb seedlings, a hose reel and a glass-walled lap pool beyond the open doorway; a plain pair of worn rubber swimming fins sits on the bench — Instead of throwing away a damaged rubber swim fin, she makes it into a little herb planter, setting a seedling into its foot pocket with one hand while her other hand steadies the fin. She raises one knee onto the bench to balance the potting tray; the movement fans aside a loose outer swim-skirt panel and reveals the upper thigh above the fully opaque fitted swim shorts. The suit stays secure; this is a casual practical movement rather than a posed display

A quiet volcanic-island beach repair awning beside a row of folded inflatable boats, a little sand-covered workbench and distant turquoise sea in bright morning light — She has interrupted her swim to mend a pinhole in an inflatable rubber dinghy, pressing a circular rubber patch firmly with a small hand roller while her other hand steadies the tube. To reach the patch she swings one knee over the wide tube; this action folds back the loose outer pleat of her swim shorts and briefly bares more of her upper thigh, with the opaque inner swim shorts secure

a converted Victorian waterworks used as a small indoor swimming club, with cream ceramic tiles, warm greenhouse windows, a shallow practice pool and a compact clear charcoal-filter vessel beside the deck — after testing the little charcoal filter, she is laughing quietly at a large plain rubber swimming ring that is awkwardly stuck around her hips. She lifts and tilts the ring up past her torso to free herself: the equipment briefly uncovers her bare waist and the open side seams of her fitted swimsuit while the swimsuit itself remains securely fastened and dry. This is an awkward everyday equipment-removal moment, not rain, a gust, undone clothing or a slipped strap

her quiet home instrument-repair corner at dawn, a low felt-covered bench holding a single carbon-fibre cello with its strings loosened and a plain wooden chair beside it; soft daylight, no futuristic armour or military equipment — she is checking a newly repaired carbon-fibre cello bridge before breakfast, gently plucking one string to hear whether its vibration is clean. To steady the instrument she raises one bent knee onto the low chair; that practical movement folds the loose overlapping side panel of her lingerie sleep set aside and reveals the side of her upper thigh above the fully opaque shorts. The reveal comes from a lifted knee and folded fabric, not wet clothing, a gust, an undone top or a slipped strap
a bridal room — seated on a chair
her own room in a house of her element's kingdom — standing
a glass and pottery workshop with a glowing kiln — holds a magnifying glass by its handle at chest height
a chandelier ballroom at a masquerade — holds a small jar of cube salt crystals that glows faintly yellow at chest height
a city park with benches — holds an ice cream cone at chest height
